failure_modes.mode: BPR Valve Blockage due to Precipitation
failure_modes.cause: Electrophilic aromatic substitution products or salts precipitate in the high-pressure restriction zone, causing valve seizure and system overpressure or flow stoppage.
failure_modes.mitigation: Install a 5-micron inline filter upstream of the BPR and implement a back-flush protocol every 4 hours.

failure_modes.mode: Thermal Runaway due to Heat Transfer Limitation
failure_modes.cause: Although Da_thermal is low, the long residence time (23.7 min) in a narrow channel (0.75 mm) with poor external heat transfer coefficients can lead to localized hot spots if the jacket temperature control fails or solvent viscosity increases.
failure_modes.mitigation: Implement redundant temperature sensors along the coil length and set an automatic flow shutdown if T exceeds 70°C.

failure_modes.cause: At Q=0.447 mL/min and T=60°C, the solvent vapor pressure may approach the pump inlet pressure, especially if the feed reservoir is not pressurized, leading to inconsistent residence time and selectivity loss.
failure_modes.mitigation: Pressurize feed reservoirs to 0.5 bar above the solvent's vapor pressure at 60°C and use a pulse-dampening accumulator.

single_points_of_failure: BPR Valve — blockage stops all flow and risks overpressure
Single Temperature Sensor — failure leads to undetected thermal excursion
validation_experiments: Run continuous flow for 10x residence time (237 min) with product-forming conditions; monitor BPR pressure stability and inspect valve for particulate accumulation.
Perform a heat transfer coefficient test by introducing a step-change in jacket temperature and measuring the response time of the fluid temperature at the outlet to verify thermal control adequacy.
Conduct a cavitation test by gradually reducing feed reservoir pressure while monitoring pump head pressure and flow rate consistency to determine the minimum safe inlet pressure.
